values.condition: Ejection speed reported for S5-HVS1 from Hills breakup (Koposov et al. 2020); not corrected for the Galactic potential.

evidence.quote: One prominent example of HVS of Galactic Center origin is S5-HVS1, which is believed to be a ≈ 2.35 M⊙ main-sequence star ejected through the Hills breakup at speed of v_ej ≈ 1800 km s−1 (Koposov et al. 2020).

notes: S5-HVS1: the paper treats it as an already-known Galactic-center HVS from prior work and uses it as a benchmark to infer its progenitor binary (T:p10-b10, T:p15-b7), so it is classified as follow_up rather than a newly identified candidate. No Gaia identifier is supplied. The simulated binaries and their Hills-breakup products are anonymous population members without individual stellar identifiers, so they are not listed separately.

S5-HVS1: The paper reports no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, line-of-sight radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability specifically for S5-HVS1. Its only numerical S5-HVS1 quantity is the reported ejection speed v_ej ≈ 1800 km/s; I treat this as a total ejection velocity rather than a line-of-sight radial velocity because the paper does not specify a line-of-sight component. A model-dependent analytical HVS velocity of 820 km/s is also quoted for an assumed equal-mass binary with M_b = 4.7 M⊙ and a_b = 0.3 AU, but that is not an observed value for S5-HVS1, so I do not record it as a separate S5-HVS1 quantity.
